t: This is 14 Holland Park Road, a building in Kensington and Chelsea. It was designed by Philip Webb, who is sometimes called the Father of Arts and Crafts Architecture. Webb believed in what he called the art of common building, drawing on vernacular tradition. He worked alongside William Morris, Edward Burne-Jones and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, and designed a notable building for Morris himself. He also co-founded the Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings, so the house is worth a slow look.
